text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- BNDES SETS DETAILS FOR VALE SELLOFF

Brazil's National Privatization Council authorized the National Development Bank to negotiate with the states of Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul the sale of 47 percent of Urucum mining project belonging to soon-to-be-privatized Companhia Vale do Rio Doce.
-- BOZANO SPEEDS UP ITS EXPANSION ABROAD
Local investment bank Banco Bozano, Simonsen wants to expand its activities abroad and plans to open a brokerage in Singapore in the second half of the year.
-- THE TARGET IS A BUDGET PRIMARY SURPLUS OF 0.8 PCT
Approval of civil service reform and the sale of Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) would help the government meet its target of a primary budget surplus of 0.8 percent of GDP in 1997.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- FIESP CRITICIZES COMPROMISE WITH DEPUTIES

The president of Sao Paulo state's Industry Federation criticized an accord between President Fernando Henrique Cardoso and lawmakers allowing Lower House approval of civil service reform in a first-round vote.
-- AID TO BAMERINDUS MAY TOP 5.9 BLN REAIS

A Central Bank report reveals that HSBC Bamerindus may receive more than the 5.868 billion reais in funds from the government's PROER program to finance bank mergers and acquisitions. The report says further financing may be necessary.
O GLOBO
-- SUPREME COURT SUSPENDS SENATE'S RIGHT TO LIFT BANK SECRECY

A judge from the Supreme Federal Tribunal granted an injunction suspending the Senate's lifting of bank secrecy rights of Pedro Neiva, a former Sao Paulo mayor's office employee allegedly involved in a multi-million dollar debt scam.
-- DRUG DEALERS KILL TWO POLICEMEN AT RIO SLUM
Two policemen were killed and one was injured by drug traffickers in an ambush at a Rio slum late Wednesday.
-- Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
((-- Fatima Cristina, Sao Paulo Newsroom 5511-2485412))
